thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] ElmStreet Private VPC - high 5xx and NLB target unhealthy. Automatic paging triggered for #incidents. Suspected: NLB healthchecks failing -> customer traffic errors. Link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1809994322

ben-oncall-net: Acknowledged. I'm on call for network. Can someone pull target-group health and recent SG/NACL changes for ElmStreet tenant (dedicated-pool-elm-2)?

amy-sre: Looking now. NLB target group tg-elm-2 shows 70% failing healthchecks on port 8080. Failures originate from two AZ subnets (10.12.45.0/24, 10.12.46.0/24). Application logs show connection refused / timeout. No recent deploys in app side.

liz-eng-ops: Customer CS flagged 5xx spike from their product team ~02:06Z. They said they recently tightened outbound NACL rules in their VPC to block some egress ranges.

jai-cs: Confirmed from ElmStreet: we applied a NACL change at ~02:04Z to block a set of IP ranges used for internal services. We didn't expect it to affect the loadbalancer.

ben-oncall-net: Audit shows a security change: NACL acl-0e4f modified at 2026-03-17T02:04:20Z by elm-admin. Also see a security-group delta on sg-0a9b (web-target-sg) at 02:05:05Z created by their automation. Likely blocking NLB node healthcheck source IPs.

amy-sre: Confirmed. Healthcheck source IPs for internal NLB are node-private IPs; because this is a Private NLB, healthchecks come from the NLB worker ENIs in each AZ. If customer NACL/SG blocks those, targets go unhealthy.

marta-eng: We have a pre-authorized rollback path: two options - (A) ask ElmStreet to revert their NACL change (preferred), (B) apply a temporary SG allow for the NLB healthcheck CIDRs on their target SG. We can also failover traffic to their fallback ALB in us-west-2 if needed.

ben-oncall-net: Paging ElmStreet primary contact now (via phone). Meanwhile, we should prepare mitigation steps. Who can execute a temporary SG allow?

liz-eng-ops: I can run a temporary change on their target SG if they approve. Proposed rule: allow inbound TCP 8080 from the NLB node ENI CIDR blocks (we list them in the runbook). Command (internal runbook snippet):

```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a9b --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.12.100.0/22 --profile redwood-admin
```

Note: replace CIDR with exact NLB node CIDRs for ElmStreet (runbook/automated discovery can populate). This is temporary; will be revoked after incident.

jai-cs: ElmStreet confirms they can rollback the NACL but need 10min to test. They asked us to apply the temporary SG allow in the meantime to restore traffic quickly. Authorize on our side only after customer's explicit consent.

ben-oncall-net: I have verbal consent from ElmStreet to apply temporary SG rule. Proceeding.

incident-bot: Action logged: temporary SG allow requested by ben-oncall-net. Creating change ticket CHG-1809994322.

liz-eng-ops: Applied temporary SG allow for NLB nodes -> sg-0a9b ingress tcp/8080 from 10.12.100.0/22. Monitoring.

amy-sre: Seeing target group health recover within 30s. 200 responses returning from app nodes. 5xx rate dropping to baseline. ElmStreet reports client requests succeeding again.

dns-bot: Note: ElmStreet uses a Route53 private hosted zone with weighted records across internal endpoints. No DNS change required for this mitigation. If we needed failover, we can enact the pre-approved weighted shift to alb-elm-fallback internal.

marta-eng: Recommend next steps: 1) ElmStreet reverts NACL delta, 2) verify for 10m, 3) we revoke the temporary SG rule and monitor for 15m. If any regression, we fail traffic to fallback ALB.

jai-cs: ElmStreet rolled back the NACL change at 02:18Z. They will run a small test suite now and report in 5m.

ben-oncall-net: Rolling temp SG rule removal in 2m to confirm customer's change holds.

liz-eng-ops: Revoked temporary SG allow. (aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a9b --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.12.100.0/22)

amy-sre: Targets remained healthy after SG revoke. App 200s stable. 5xx spike cleared.

ben-oncall-net: Confirming with ElmStreet. They report all services OK. No further client errors.

incident-bot: Incident resolved for ElmStreet Private VPC NLB healthcheck -> root cause: customer-managed NACL change blocked NLB node healthchecks. Mitigation: temporary SG allow + customer rollback of NACL. Creating follow-up ticket for postmortem and runbook update: add a guardrail to warn on NACL changes that block internal NLB healthcheck CIDRs.

marta-eng: I'll own the postmortem and runbook update (add automated detection of target-group Unhealthy->NACL delta and a one-click rollback suggestion).

jai-cs: Customer CS will schedule a short call with ElmStreet network team to review safe change windows and add a pre-change checklist.

ben-oncall-net: Closing incident thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
